From cd9d9377ed235b294a492a094e1666178a5e78fd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2021 12:28:31 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] media: v4l2-ioctl.c: readbuffers depends on
 V4L2_CAP_READWRITE

If V4L2_CAP_READWRITE is not set, then readbuffers must be set to 0,
otherwise v4l2-compliance will complain.

A note on the Fixes tag below: this patch does not really fix that commit,
but it can be applied from that commit onwards. For older code there is no
guarantee that device_caps is set, so even though this patch would apply,
it will not work reliably.

Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
Fixes: 049e684f2de9 (media: v4l2-dev: fix WARN_ON(!vdev->device_caps))
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+huawei@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c b/drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c
index 31d0109ce5a8..69b74d0e8a90 100644
--- a/drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c
+++ b/drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c
@@ -2090,6 +2090,7 @@ static int v4l_prepare_buf(const struct v4l2_ioctl_ops *ops,
 static int v4l_g_parm(const struct v4l2_ioctl_ops *ops,
 				struct file *file, void *fh, void *arg)
 {
+	struct video_device *vfd = video_devdata(file);
 	struct v4l2_streamparm *p = arg;
 	v4l2_std_id std;
 	int ret = check_fmt(file, p->type);
@@ -2101,7 +2102,8 @@ static int v4l_g_parm(const struct v4l2_ioctl_ops *ops,
 	if (p->type != V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE &&
 	    p->type != V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE_MPLANE)
 		return -EINVAL;
-	p->parm.capture.readbuffers = 2;
+	if (vfd->device_caps & V4L2_CAP_READWRITE)
+		p->parm.capture.readbuffers = 2;
 	ret = ops->vidioc_g_std(file, fh, &std);
 	if (ret == 0)
 		v4l2_video_std_frame_period(std, &p->parm.capture.timeperframe);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/media/v4l2-core/v4l2-ioctl.c`**
- A new variable `struct video_device *vfd` is introduced to hold the video device data retrieved from the file descriptor.
- The logic for setting `p->parm.capture.readbuffers` is modified:
  - It is now conditionally set to `2` only if the `V4L2_CAP_READWRITE` capability is present in `vfd->device_caps`.
  - If `V4L2_CAP_READWRITE` is not set, `p->parm.capture.readbuffers` will not be explicitly set, which defaults it to `0`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification ensures that the `readbuffers` value is dependent on the device's capabilities, specifically the `V4L2_CAP_READWRITE` flag. This change addresses a compliance issue with `v4l2-compliance`, ensuring that if the device does not support read/write operations, the `readbuffers` value is appropriately set to `0`. This relationship enhances the robustness of the code by preventing potential warnings or errors when the device capabilities are not aligned with the expected buffer settings.

Signed-off-by: Hans Verkuil <hverkuil-cisco@xs4all.nl>
Fixes: 049e684f2de9 (media: v4l2-dev: fix WARN_ON(!vdev->device_caps))
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+huawei@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the fact that the `readbuffers` parameter was being set to a default value of `2` without checking if the `V4L2_CAP_READWRITE` capability was enabled. This could lead to compliance issues with `v4l2-compliance`, as devices that do not support read/write operations would not be able to handle a non-zero `readbuffers` value, resulting in warnings or errors.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int v4l_g_parm(const struct v4l2_ioctl_ops *ops,
 				struct file *file, void *fh, void *arg)
 {
+	struct video_device *vfd = video_devdata(file);
 	struct v4l2_streamparm *p = arg;
 	v4l2_std_id std;
 	int ret = check_fmt(file, p->type);
 
 	if (ret)
 		return ret;
 	if (ops->vidioc_g_parm)
 		return ops->vidioc_g_parm(file, fh, p);
 	if (p->type != V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE &&
 	    p->type != V4L2_BUF_TYPE_VIDEO_CAPTURE_MPLANE)
 		return -EINVAL;
-	p->parm.capture.readbuffers = 2;
+	if (vfd->device_caps & V4L2_CAP_READWRITE)
+		p->parm.capture.readbuffers = 2;
 	ret = ops->vidioc_g_std(file, fh, &std);
 	if (ret == 0)
 		v4l2_video_std_frame_period(std, &p->parm.capture.timeperframe);
 	return ret;
 }
